proposals.before: Wang Zhixing, style name Kuangjian, was from Wen in Huazhou.
proposals.after: Wang Zhixing, style name Kuangjian, was from Wen in Huaizhou.
proposals.reason: 懷州 is Huaizhou, not Huazhou; the current translation misidentifies the native place.

proposals.before: He was called Yan Zai at first, but later dropped the surname "Yan" and went by Zai alone.
proposals.after: He was called Yan Zai at first, but later dropped the generational name "Yan" and went by Zai alone.
proposals.reason: 晏 is part of the given name/generational element 晏宰, not a surname; the repair preserves the renaming.

proposals.before: Yan Zai, afterward he removed "Yan" and was known by the single name Zai.
proposals.after: Yan Zai later removed "Yan" and was known by the single name Zai.
proposals.reason: 晏 is part of the name 晏宰, not a surname; the literal should describe dropping that name element.

proposals.before: When Zhixing returned, Qun sent staff members to welcome him and ordered the soldiers to enter in armor season by season.
proposals.after: When Zhixing returned, Qun sent staff members to welcome him and ordered the soldiers to enter in armor.
proposals.reason: 季甲 is not an idiom meaning season by season here; the context requires entering in armor.

decisions.reason: Chinese 懷州溫人 names the native place as Wen in Huaizhou; Huazhou would be 華州, so the proposed Huaizhou correction matches the source.
晏宰，後去「晏」，獨名宰 drops the name element 晏 from 晏宰; calling 晏 a surname invents a false family name, while “generational name” correctly identifies the dropped given-name element.
The literal already says he removed “Yan” and was known by the single name Zai, without calling 晏 a surname; changing “afterward he” to “later” is only stylistic and does not repair meaning.

令士季甲而入 means the soldiers were ordered to enter armored; reading 季 as “season by season” invents a temporal sense absent from the reception scene, and dropping that phrase restores the armor sense already in the idiomatic line.
